reading: Two marker cells sit diagonally outside two corners of a hollow square. The square's interior is split into four quadrants; each marker colours the quadrant next to its own corner and the quadrant diagonally opposite, making a 2x2 checkerboard.

slots.region: interior of the one rectangular outline (frame), cut into 4 equal quadrants
slots.colours: the two marker colours outside the frame
slots.assignment: the quadrant nearest each marker and its diagonal opposite get that marker's colour

why: every interior cell takes the colour of the marker nearest its quadrant or of its diagonal partner; frame and markers unchanged

reading: A strip of stacked colour columns is a key read left to right. One shape occurs in some of the key colours stacked vertically; copies of the shape are added above and below so the stack runs top to bottom in key order, and the key is erased.

slots.key: the multi-colour strip of vertical bars; its column order is the colour order
slots.unit: the repeated shape (all copies share one shape, one colour each)
slots.placement: copies stacked vertically at the same columns, shape height apart, aligned with the existing copies

why: the output stack's colours from top to bottom equal the key's colours from left to right; existing copies stay in place

reading: A hollow rectangle holds four coloured cells in its inner corners. They are removed and each colour reappears just outside the rectangle at the diagonally opposite outer corner.

slots.subject: the four single cells in the inner corners of the outline
slots.target: the cell diagonally outside the opposite corner of the outline (180-degree rotation about the frame centre, pushed outside)

why: inner-corner colour at corner k equals the outer diagonal cell at corner opposite k; outline unchanged

reading: The most common colour of the 3x3 grid stays; every other cell becomes grey 5.
why: every non-background (non-majority) cell becomes 5; background cells unchanged

reading: Each 2x2 grey block gets four diagonal corner cells: 1 at top-left, 2 at top-right, 3 at bottom-left, 4 at bottom-right.
why: every 2x2 object gets the identical 4x4 corner pattern 1..2/3..4 around it; all other cells unchanged

reading: A grid of grey separator lines is sprinkled with noise of one colour. All noise is removed, separator lines are restored to grey, and every crossing of a horizontal and vertical separator takes the noise colour.

slots.separators: rows and columns that are (mostly) grey 5 lines
slots.crossings: cells where a separator row meets a separator column get the noise colour
slots.rest: panel cells become 0, separator cells become 5

why: output = clean separator lattice in 5 with noise colour exactly at line intersections; nothing else coloured

reading: The output is twice as wide; each patterned row continues its horizontal period across the extra width (not a plain side-by-side copy).

slots.rule: each row's minimal horizontal period is extended to the new width; empty rows stay empty

why: every output row is the input row's period repeated to width 2W

reading: A lattice of 3x3 rings has pairs of same-coloured marker cells. For each pair, the bounding box of the two markers is snapped outward to the lattice gap lines; its outline is drawn along those gap rows/columns in the marker colour and the centre of every ring inside is filled with that colour.

slots.markers: two cells of one non-lattice colour, per colour
slots.box: smallest rectangle of lattice gap rows/columns enclosing both markers
slots.draw: outline on the box's gap lines in marker colour; ring centres inside the box get marker colour
slots.rest: marker cells absorbed; ring cells (8) unchanged

why: per colour pair, outline lies exactly on the enclosing gap lines and only ring centres inside are recoloured

reading: Coloured cells in the top row each start a full vertical line of their colour down the grid; where the line crosses a block of the same colour it shows the background colour instead.

slots.line: the whole column from top to bottom border
slots.colour: source colour, except background colour where the crossed cell already has the source colour

why: in each source column, every cell is the source colour unless the input cell had that colour, then it is background; other columns unchanged

reading: Two framed panels: the left one holds coloured bars on its background, the right one is empty. Each bar is copied into the right panel at the same rows: bars touching the left margin go to the right panel's left margin, bars touching the right margin go to its right margin, and full-width bars stretch across the right panel.
verb: copy into panel with edge alignment

slots.target panel: the empty panel of another background colour
slots.alignment: each shape keeps its rows and its 1-cell margin to the left or right panel edge; full-width shapes stretch to the target's width minus margins

why: every target row equals the source row's shapes re-aligned to the same edge margins; source panel and borders unchanged
